content.title: About
content.content: Pickled seaweed is made from dried and then re‑hydrated marine algae, usually from the Porphyra (nori) or Laminaria families. It has a distinctive salty‑sour flavor, a crisp texture, and a vivid green color. The product is common in Asian cuisines, used in salads, sushi rolls, and as a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Seaweed is one of the richest natural sources of iodine, essential for thyroid function.
In Japan, nori is a staple food and appears in more than 70 % of all sushi rolls.
There are over 10,000 species of marine algae, but only a small fraction are edible.
Pickling helps preserve nutrients and extends shelf life to several months.
In traditional Korean cuisine, fermented seaweed (miyeok) is served as a side dish.

items.title: Rich in iodine
items.content: Iodine supports the production of thyroid hormones that regulate metabolism.

items.title: High in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is important for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Seaweed contains polyphenols and carotenoids that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It provides calcium, iron, magnesium, and potassium, which are vital for various bodily functions.

items.title: Excess iodine
items.content: Too much iodine can disrupt thyroid function, especially in susceptible individuals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Pickled seaweed is salty; people with hypertension should limit their intake.

items.title: Seaweed allergy
items.content: Rare, but some individuals may experience allergic reactions.

items.title: Contaminants
items.content: Algae can accumulate heavy metals from the ocean; choose products from reputable sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pickled seaweed can be eaten straight as a snack, added to salads, sushi rolls, soups, or used as a garnish. It is often rinsed briefly to reduce excess brine before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a sealed container in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C. Shelf life is typically 3–6 months. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
